articles.title: Crypto Long & Short: What this year's $972 million crypto hacks actually tell us about security
articles.snippet: In this week's Crypto Long & Short, Immunefi's Mitchell Amador writes that most of 2026's stolen crypto is leaving through keys, signers and governance, not contract bugs, and explains why “we were audited” was never the same as “we are safe.”

articles.title: Russia charges Telegram founder Pavel Durov with aiding terrorism
articles.snippet: The charges could result in life imprisonment, escalating an investigation that has already led to over 100 million rubles in fines for the platform this year.

articles.title: 'Anything remotely dovish' from Fed could be good for bitcoin, says analyst
articles.snippet: Traders are divided on whether the Fed will hike rates, but analysts said crypto may be less exposed than AI-driven tech stocks.

articles.title: Telegram founder Pavel Durov internationally wanted, Russia’s FSB says
articles.snippet: Russia’s FSB says Telegram founder Pavel Durov faces a terrorism-related charge and an international arrest warrant, while a separate French case remains open.

articles.title: Trump teleprompter operator accused over Kalshi bets leaves government: AP
articles.snippet: Gabriel Perez, who was accused of profiting from Kalshi bets tied to President Donald Trump’s speeches, is no longer employed by the federal government.
